input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
input.rationale: Section 11.3 is the only audit/inspection-type right binding Customer: IBM may "investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty at will. There is no frequency cap, no advance notice requirement (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt before restricting access or removing Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours or independent-auditor requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to Customer systems — while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request. Unlimited and unannounced audits are the playbook walk-away, so we inserted the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access) as a single proviso in § 11.3, leaving IBM's substantive remedies untouched.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits on IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added standard limits to IBM's investigation right: no more than one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and no access to our systems. As drafted the right is unlimited and unannounced, which our playbook treats as a walk-away; we can accept 15 days' notice and a 10% cost-shift threshold as a fallback.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. No such investigation will include direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records, and Customer may satisfy any such investigation by providing relevant information off-site.
